name: ormar-e2c8a526-blind28-ots
instr:
# ormar answers wrong on saving, querying, ordering and dumping — without a test suite

A fresh checkout of this library for storing objects in a database now answers differently at almost every step, and the damage is scattered rather than concentrated. Nothing about the database changed and nothing about the calling code changed: the same declarations, writes and queries that used to be handled correctly are now handled wrongly, and in several places something that used to be refused is quietly accepted while something that used to work fails outright. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits.

Start where a class is declared. Asking for an integer primary key that is also encrypted, with a secret and a backend supplied, is now accepted in silence, where such a declaration used to be refused with a definition error while the class body was still being built. Declaring a column restricted to a set of choices and handing it an empty list where a type listing permitted members belongs is likewise waved through instead of being refused at that same moment. When two concrete classes each inherit the same pointer to a shared owner from an abstract parent, the two reverse collections installed on that owner no longer stay apart, so asking the owner for the entries of each child either errors or brings back the wrong ones.
